# Heading

A heading's text style, independent of the HTML tag it renders. The tag tracks the ambient level from `HeadingContextProvider`, so moving a heading to a different place in the page never requires touching its `size`.

Also asked as: title, headline.

**Import:** `import { Heading } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/Heading/Heading.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/Heading/Heading.stories.jsx` — Overview, Sizes, OverridesTheTag, NestedContext, InverseColor, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, NotAControl

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/Heading/Heading.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Heading` for every heading in the product: a page title, a section
header, a card title. Never style plain text to look like a heading: a
sighted-only "heading" breaks navigation by heading for anyone using
assistive technology.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write headings that say what the section is about. | Write headings that repeat the page title. |
| Use sentence case. | Use title case or all caps. |
| Keep a heading to a short phrase. | Write a heading that wraps past two lines. |
| Choose `size` for the look and let the level pick the tag. | Pick a larger size to make a heading seem more important than its level. |

## Best practices

### Choose `size` for the look. {#choose-size-for-the-look}

`size` is required, and it is separate from the tag the context picks.

Do: Pass the size the spot needs and let the level pick the tag.
Don't: Pick a tag to get a size, which breaks the outline.

### Use `as="div"` for a label that is not a heading. {#use-as-div-for-a-label-that-is-not-a-heading}

Do: Heading style with no heading meaning.
Don't: A real heading that screen reader users meet in the outline.

### Let the ground set the ink. {#let-the-ground-set-the-ink}

Do: The inverse color on a dark ground.
Don't: The default ink on a dark ground, which barely reads.

## Accessibility

- **The tag is the real heading level**, not a visual effect: a screen
  reader's "jump to heading" list is built from the actual tag, which is why
  nesting through `HeadingContextProvider` matters more than it looks.
- **`as` can break the outline if misused.** Overriding the tag to something
  that isn't `h1`–`h6` (like `div` or `span`) removes it from the heading
  outline entirely: correct for a styled label, wrong for an actual section
  title.
- **Match the ink to the ground.** Pass
  `color.text.inverse` or `color.text.warning.inverse` when the heading sits
  on a dark ground; the token resolves the right ink in every color mode.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `as` | enum | — | Overrides the HTML element the heading renders as. |
| `size` | enum | — | The text style. Required: a heading with no size is not a heading. |
| `color` | enum | — | Applies inverse text color automatically when the ground is dark. |
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `testId` | string | — | — |
| `children` | node (required) | — | — |
